title: Shared Photo Consent Checklist v1.0
description: An open, machine-readable checklist for consent, capture, reveal, storage and deletion in one-phone group photo experiences.
methodology: Victor Laybats authored the checklist from Sealed’s documented one-phone workflow, safety boundaries and public data-handling disclosures. The criteria are product-independent questions with a concrete evidence request. The release does not certify Sealed or any other photo application.
limitations: This is a practical review framework, not legal advice, a security audit or proof of consent in a particular event. Consent depends on context and can be withdrawn. Laws, age rules, venue policies, operating-system backups and third-party sharing can change the correct process.

sources.name: Sealed safety, consent and evidence methodology

criteria.criterion: The host states the purpose of the photo activity.
criteria.rationale: People can make a better choice when the intended ritual and audience are explicit.
criteria.evidencePrompt: Record the invitation or opening explanation.

criteria.criterion: Participation is optional and refusal has no penalty.
criteria.rationale: Group pressure can undermine a nominal choice.
criteria.evidencePrompt: Document the non-participation path and host wording.

criteria.criterion: The group knows which device will capture and store photos.
criteria.rationale: A shared phone concentrates custody and access in one place.
criteria.evidencePrompt: Identify the device owner and who can unlock it.

criteria.criterion: The reveal time and audience are stated in advance.
criteria.rationale: Delayed capture should not hide when or with whom images will be viewed.
criteria.evidencePrompt: Record the timer and planned audience.

criteria.criterion: Rules for minors and guardians are explicit.
criteria.rationale: Age and safeguarding requirements need a separate decision, not an assumption.
criteria.evidencePrompt: Record the age rule and guardian process.

criteria.criterion: The device gives a clear indication when a photo is taken.
criteria.rationale: A blind preview should not become covert capture.
criteria.evidencePrompt: Observe shutter feedback, screen state and sound behavior.

criteria.criterion: A person can decline a specific photo after joining the activity.
criteria.rationale: Joining once should not remove control over later moments.
criteria.evidencePrompt: Demonstrate how a participant signals no capture.

criteria.criterion: Sensitive spaces and situations are excluded.
criteria.rationale: Bathrooms, changing areas, distress and incapacity require firm boundaries.
criteria.evidencePrompt: Inspect host rules and in-product safety guidance.

criteria.criterion: The product does not imply that hidden preview prevents misuse.
criteria.rationale: A concealed preview cannot stop another camera, coercion or later screenshots.
criteria.evidencePrompt: Review claims about privacy and secrecy.

criteria.criterion: The group renews consent before the shared reveal.
criteria.rationale: Circumstances may change between capture and viewing.
criteria.evidencePrompt: Record the prompt or host check immediately before reveal.

criteria.criterion: The reveal can be paused or stopped.
criteria.rationale: A participant needs an immediate control if an image causes concern.
criteria.evidencePrompt: Demonstrate pause, exit and device-lock behavior.

criteria.criterion: An unwanted image has a deletion path.
criteria.rationale: Delayed surprise should not override removal after viewing.
criteria.evidencePrompt: Test deletion before any save or export.

criteria.criterion: Screenshot and screen-recording limits are disclosed.
criteria.rationale: Software may not be able to detect or prevent secondary capture.
criteria.evidencePrompt: Check the notice and test operating-system capture.

criteria.criterion: Saving a photo is a separate action from revealing it.
criteria.rationale: Viewing within an app should not silently create another library copy.
criteria.evidencePrompt: Compare app storage before and after reveal and save.

criteria.criterion: Save and share actions state their destination.
criteria.rationale: Copies can move beyond the original group and retention rules.
criteria.evidencePrompt: Record the permission prompt, destination and share sheet.

criteria.criterion: Participants agree before public posting or redistribution.
criteria.rationale: Consent to capture is not automatically consent to publication.
criteria.evidencePrompt: Document the approval process for each external audience.

criteria.criterion: Local, cloud and backup storage are distinguished.
criteria.rationale: A claim of local storage can coexist with device-level backup or export.
criteria.evidencePrompt: Map app storage, system backup and any service upload.

criteria.criterion: Retention and capsule deletion are explained.
criteria.rationale: Users need to know whether opening, saving or uninstalling changes the original.
criteria.evidencePrompt: Test opening, manual deletion and uninstall behavior.

criteria.criterion: Permissions are limited to the selected function.
criteria.rationale: Camera, microphone and photo-library access have different consequences.
criteria.evidencePrompt: Record each permission, timing and fallback when denied.

criteria.criterion: The device lock and account boundary are part of the threat model.
criteria.rationale: Local content remains exposed if the shared device itself is accessible.
criteria.evidencePrompt: Document screen-lock, app-lock and guest-access behavior.

criteria.criterion: There is a visible reporting and urgent-removal route.
criteria.rationale: People need a path for harmful, unlawful or child-safety content.
criteria.evidencePrompt: Verify the public contact and response instructions.

criteria.criterion: Privacy and enjoyment claims are bounded and testable.
criteria.rationale: A product feature does not prove safety, consent quality or a better social outcome.
criteria.evidencePrompt: Classify each claim and record the evidence and limitations.
